longDays.title: Wildwood — vertical build
longDays.desc: Week 1 of the long-day progression. In-town, smooth tread.

longDays.title: Angels Rest → Devil's Rest loop
longDays.desc: 10.7 mi, Columbia River Gorge. Talus and exposed switchbacks. No timed-use permit in 2026. Objective is the descent, not the summit — watch the descent HR gap.

longDays.title: Table Mountain
longDays.desc: 8.4 mi from Bonneville. Heartbreak Ridge drops 700 ft in half a mile on loose talus — the quad-wrecker rehearsal. Steep meadow exposure near the summit.

longDays.title: Three Sisters Loop
longDays.desc: First real overnight and multi-day exposure — a good spot to try a short deliberate sleep stop.

longDays.title: DELOAD — Wildwood
longDays.desc: Deload week: 60-70% of block targets. Recovery from the Three Sisters multi-day. Keep the frequency, cut the duration.

longDays.title: COURSE RECON — Norway Pass → Mount Margaret
longDays.desc: 11 mi out-and-back, high point 5,780 ft. This is Bigfoot course miles 56 back toward 37, and Mount Margaret is the HIGH POINT OF THE RACE. Manual: 'Best views of the course, recommend running in daylight if possible.' NW Forest Pass or $5 day-use; no backcountry permit for day hiking. Water at Bear Camp (mi 4.1) is unreliable late season — carry it. No dogs. WEATHER PLAN: FR 99 and the Norway Pass trailhead close with snow and mid-October is late. Check mshinstitute.org/current-conditions the week before. If the road is shut, SWAP with Oct 24 — do Elk/Kings today and try the recon again the following weekend.
longDays.fallback: Swap with Oct 24 (Elk / Kings) if FR 99 is closed.

longDays.title: Elk Mountain / Kings Mountain traverse
longDays.desc: 10.9 mi, Tillamook State Forest. Exposed narrow ridge with scrambling and a fixed rope — closest thing in Block 1 to Blue Lake → Coldwater Lake. Elk Mtn climbs 2,080 ft in 1.5 mi. Coast Range, high point 3,226 ft — no snow risk in October, which is why it's the recon's backstop. IF YOU SWAPPED: this is the second and last recon attempt. If FR 99 is still shut, do Nesmith Point (~3,800 ft, similar day) and let the recon wait for summer 2027 — Klickitat → Twin Sisters matters more anyway and wants 2027 conditions.
longDays.fallback: If used as the second recon attempt and FR 99 is still closed: Nesmith Point, ~3,800 ft.

longDays.title: Mount Defiance
longDays.desc: 11.6 mi, the hardest day hike in the region — 3,000 ft in three miles. Biggest day of the block. Late in its season at 4,959 ft: if there's snow up high, swap to Nesmith Point (~3,800 ft).

longDays.title: Run the Rock 25K
longDays.desc: Block 1 checkpoint. 25K rather than the 50K: running tolerance is 12 mi/wk and even a perfect 10%/week ramp only reaches ~26 by today, against 31 running miles for the 50K. Finish strong rather than survived.

longDays.title: DELOAD — Angels Rest
longDays.desc: Deload week: 60-70% of block targets. Recovery from Run the Rock. Easy effort, half the usual long day.

longDays.title: Dog Mountain
longDays.desc: Steep and relentless. Permit is spring weekends only — free in November. First night-hours sessions should be landing this month too.

longDays.title: Elk / Kings — BENCHMARK REPEAT
longDays.desc: Same course as Oct 24, six weeks later. This is a measurement, not a workout: compare time, descent HR gap, and how the last hour felt. It tells you whether Block 1 worked.

longDays.title: DELOAD — taper into Frozen Trail
longDays.desc: Deload week: 60-70%. Taper into the Dec 12 Frozen Trail 50K that closes Block 1. Short and controlled.

longDays.title: Frozen Trail Run Fest 50K
longDays.desc: Block 1 checkpoint. Block question: can you sustain a full day on feet and descend hard without wrecking your quads?
